said he wd see K next day, quite agreeing
that something must be done at once. S [?]
rang up Alcron now well after 11 to find Kundt
still here with the our young men. W remarking
that when he left there were at the chocolate
stage but that by now they must be at beer
+ sandwiches! So the apptment was fixed

It is very nice staying at Legation. We are on
the big drawingroom floor a very large 2 bedded
room with large bath room across the landing
from which a door leads into garden. The Minister's
rooms are on the floor below where small
drawingroom + dining room are. Below him
again is Chancellery.
W, slept splendidly + feels better at once
Saturday. 3.
This was to have been a great shoot for W, but he
had neither inclination or time to give. Mr Peto
went + Mrs + I joined for lunch. The Minister
was to have gone but he stayed in order to put
pressure on B in accordance with instructions.
Mrs P + I were fetched by Mme Cermac. He is a
sort of Grand Venen, for this democratic Gov:
owns large territories, variously acquired, with
first rate shooting which the various Gov: officers
seem greatly to enjoy. This was certainly a very
well run affair. Quite 100 beaters, an
elaborate lunch in a tent 3 sides open
8 guns - all very pleasant + and a lovely day.
This was mainly shooting farm lands.
A great fruit district. The day was delicious
sunny + nicely warm. Geoffrey shot 40 odd birds before
lunch

the morning bag being 310. I left immediately after
not knowing what W was doing. Found he had
again gone to the President. He tried to rub in what
the Minister had already said with force. B inclined to
urge that his country is keeping Europe safe for
democracy to which W replies you cant do that by
committing suicide. All along he has felt B under-
-estimated what a war wd mean to his country.
W's constant text is "anything is better than war."
We started off for the Cardinal Archbishops at
I am writing on Tuesday. about 6 or so. to Brezany
one of his country palaces near Prague.
It is a curious looking house built round an open
court. The gallery to 1st floor running round
three sides of the court is glazed. There our bed-
rooms were, but we ascended to the reception
rooms up a covered stair but along an
open gallery. Cold enough even now. But I gather
he never comes in winter.
This was a delightful visit, We were charmed
with the Cardinal. He received us with sec:
+ another cleric at the door dressed in his
beautiful red robe with a very lovely cross of
emeralds and diamonds, + made a formal
little speech in German welcoming us + speaking
of the honour done him by our visit. He escorted

us to our rooms all en suite Hunter too. The bath-
room was beyond us, the directions in chzeck.
+ we never ventured on a bath. We had dinner
almost at once - going through 2 or 3 bare
rooms to the dining room where we fared sumpt-
uously, no lack of food or drink or smokes. The
company included the Petos + young Count Czernin
who is 1/2 English + is a useful interpreter. He is
in the F. O. the Cardinals secretary + a Professor
of Art also in orders + I think another,
we just conversed after dinner- Only Professor
was quite bright. I was seated opposite to the Cardinal
W on one side of him Mrs Peto on the other so she
had the hard work during dinner. His German was
not very clear + I cant yet say I understand
every word even when spoken distinctly.
He had his little stories to tell + enjoyed a joke + told me
more than once how he thanked the good God for
Lord R + how he prayed for him.
On Sunday W slept for hours + only about 20 to 12
did we assemble for a little carriage drive
in the woods. Quite pleasant but weather bad
The ubiquitous Franzi who turned up on Sunday
+ Count Czernin sat on the little seats of
2 little phaetons + an estate man in air
box, the Petos went in one + we in another

Villagers as usual thronged to see us +
raised hats etc.
The Cardinal had to go + consecrate a
Church built in quite modern style to
his deep regret, he thinks buildings should
ascend towards God not squat rectangularly
But he had 500 children to give little pictures
to which he loves to do. + anyhow now the
poor people have their chuch which formerly
they lacked.
At lunch I had a new neighbour the senior Canon
+ Chancellor of the Cardial. He was a jolly fellow
+ almost at once asked if we couldnt play
bridge. He adores it + so seldom has the chance
He was so sad that Count Czernin was the
only possible interpreter for W's conversation
with the Cardinal, because where cd we get
our 4th. However it had to be + W + the Cardinal
retired to his private room + had a good talk
W, rather sad to find young Czernin talking
of war, better have it now + get it over etc.
However he got well snubbed + the Cardinal
entirely agreed that of all thingst war was the worst.
He asked if he could help W, he is a great personal
friend of Benes, should he write him a letter
What shd he say? 'Just that' said W +

he said he would + that the Senior Canon shd take
it straight to the Castle that evening.
Meantime Geoffrey Peto nobly came to the rescue
+ he spent the wet afternoon playing very bad
bridge for love in the Cardinals room!
After tea we left. W likes to get back one never
knows what will turn up next.
The Cardinal gave W lots of presents books of
pictures a little silver gilt Madonna +
a little wooden copy of the charming statue
of St Wencenlaus in the chapel of the
Cathedral here. He gave me a bouquet.
We all liked this good kindly man. who seems
to love everyone, he is miserable over the
hatred that now prevails in this country.
It is fairly recent that Gov: + RC Church
(75 to 80% of pop: are R.C.) are on good terms. My
own recollection of 1922 when I was here was
that the Gov: were trying to start a new Nat:
Church, activated by hatred of anything belonging
to the old German regime + that one of the
features of this Czech Nat Church was the
abolition of celibacy of the clergy. I did tentatively
ask some one abt it + gather that its adherents
are falling away + returning to ordinary R.C.
Any how Benes + Cardinal Archbishop are now friends.

5 - 12 September
Monday.
Another pleasant night at Legation.
We came in early to Alcron. We dined alone
with the Minister, we dont for long get away
from discussion of the people here + the
problems. but we go to bed early.
I went off in morning with the Lord Mayor
Dr Zenkl to see the famous Masaryk Homes.
They are a regular colony of modern flat
roofed verandahed buildings with huge
chimney for central heating, huge gardens
greenhouses, swimming pools etc On the way
Dr Zenkl gave me a description of it
all + of the motives which led him to throw
himself into this work, to cure Communism
by showing sympathy + readiness to share
advantages of pleasures medical knowledge
+ general amenties of life with the less
fortunate. A kind little man. We arrived
+ I was solemny introduced to 10 or 12 authorities
male + female + one woman in particular who
talked incorrect but intelligible English showed
me round. It appears to be an institution of
aged poor, incapable men + women,
childen who need special care, feeding
up, who come from alcoholic homes, orphans

etc + who stay 6 mon or a year or as is necessary
for health. They are sometimes boarded out if
homes unfit to take them back. The whole thing is
magnificently done. I dont wonder they are fond of it
but it strikes one as very extravagant. There is
also I learn criticism of the quarters of the aged poor
who would so much rather have their own little fire
to cook on + be alone than to have institutional meals
They all seem very well fed! I was made to go through
every division of the feeble minded, including the entirely
hopeless idiots very painful one can only admire the
nurses who attend to them. I was told that they change
them frequently.
The equipment seemed to me first rate + ones only
criticism wd be how can they possibly afford it +
is th [--] not out of all for future to other social needs.
Lunched with Geoffrey P to meet Clary's
Madame Carr wife of American Minister came to tea
+ chattered the whole time. W + I sat silent no effort
at all for us. She was very agreeable indeed.

+ no one had such influence with Benes. Poor man

So Neville [] Neville then said if that is

As it was he came back with nothing

but a sort of ultimatum from Hitler + later

Next day Wednesday [] Parliment

W went down to Puddephat for Saturday night + came

Lell had to pay on Hs W's presents + [--] my doll
escaped because he didnt know he had it + I
didnt tell him because Margie got hers in free

Crisis continued
+France + Italy saying he could not believe H wd

the House with more detail on Wednesday 28th

Neville gave a short summary of W's report
when beginning his speech + then went on
to describe all he had done + tried to do.
Much as I have written it. When he got
to the point that at this eleventh hour

again we are told that the house went

But he says until we have got agreement on

The enthusiasm for P. M. on his return was unbounded
People quite clearly really thought a war might come
But now that crisis is over already
great deal of ignorant + to my mind really
dishonest criticism is rife. I hope + believe more
among the politicians + party men than "man in the

Archie Sinclair + Atlee ill informed + very
unworthy in their criticism which in fact amounts

They forget altogether the injustices to the Sudetens,
the artificiality of C/Slovakia the faults of its rulers
+ above all they forget that no foreign assistance
cd have saved that country had Hitler chosen to
march in
But for my part I cant understand why
people were so afraid. The one thing that
emerges clearly is that none of great powers
Eng: France Germany or Italy want war +
Certainly, the reception given by German people
to the 4 statesmen showed their feelings
Maurois who called to see W on Wednesday first week of Oct: Thursday told us
that Daladier was immensely impressed by

his reception that he came back + said to his Cabinet
"They dont hate us" they liked me!"
Also I have never yet got an answer as to how
the war ever starte would start.
H wd march in if Czechs resisted he might over
run the country, but whatever he did no one
could get there to help except after long delays
+ getting permission from Rumania - Also when
W asked the French minister at Prague how they wd

But the country was very panicy and one
hears more + tales of ridiculous panicy ARP

of children without guardians to be dumped
down with no adequate arrangements
in already overcrowded villages. At Doxford
Dudley came round one day to try on masks,
+ he fitted the household but I told him he
neednt bother abt me, I said who's going
to waste bombs on us here? Oh he said I
expect they'd all be a bit "lost" if others

Crisis
were getting gas masks + they left out.

We returned to Doxford on Friday morning 23rd.
W felt he must stand by for a few days +
he also was busy getting out his report. I

advise cession - material as he put

On the Thursday Jan Masaryk looked in
W suddenly realized he had let N.C have

Poor Jan very upset. He could not bear the

24th Sept:
I got Louie to bring Brand over for week end
+ Kenneth + Mrs Wescher turned up for Sunday.
Louie in great form tho' her back had begun to
trouble her a little. Brand rather frail but
bright + wisely resting a good deal.
Kenneth was in very good form deeply interested

Brand went + saw Hew on Sunday + Louie

Hew better but still very unwell, nervous condition not

Monday 26 - 31st
W + I went up on Monday night. He wanted to
do his Bank + I Mrs. Griar in hopes she cd help
my very tiresome cold.
This was week of 'crisis'.
George got anxious about Philippa + like nearly all
London parents wanted to pack her off so she +

as good as gold + fast asreep in no time after her

+ Paula were still there. K still doing her cure.
Garry in very good form gave me a great[-] welcome

The P. M broad cast on Tuesday 27th before meeting

tell me they never heard anything so despairing!
We listened in in the drawingroom-

whether Belgium wd have been right not to fight in 1914.
The man is idiotic, but unfortunately
it appeared that nearly all these silly women

In evening W went to a Goldsmith's dinner

+ seemed to have had a great reception + to

I got John Rowlatt + Janet + George + Ruth

Thursday 20
I went with Mrs B - L to lunch at our 30 Lunch

Saturday.
For me hairdressing all morning

In evening went to concert for Marie Curie
with Lister Harrison who came to dine
Dolly + Mrs Rathbone whom we picked up after.
W + Leslie immersed in Estate duty + business

London.
It was essential for W to have the outstanding
claims of Inland Revenue settled before he
took office so W Leslie has been very energetic
+ with a push from Horace Wilson + Billy Brown
the whole thing has been done quickly.
W says Lell drove a good bargain + got on
very well with the chaps which made things
easier. So I gather the final arrangement
tho' not as good as they hoped is better
than they feared. Meantime with markets
so terribly low, Walter begins to wonder if
he will be 1d better off when all is paid up.
But I trust he is unduly pessimistic. Of course
he has given away a substantial amount
to the children. He now fears he cant
keep Sunbeam.
27 Thursday.
In all morning. Lell Mr Humble + Mr Forster
came to lunch and spent an hour or two
settling up things + signing. Steven
arrived from Eigg via Doxford in time to
do his part. He very soon now leaves for
his far distant travels. How we shall miss
him.
after lunch W + I looked at an impossible

house in Kensington Palace Gardens
+ then went to Franklin to buy a
wedding present for Gladys Gawshaw's daughter
+ then to my amazement W bought me
a lovely aqua marine +diamond band
for the hair. I was quite over come!
Now this evening I am alone as W is
out with Philip at Savoy + Steven with
a friend.
Friday. 28.
We have been looking at a possible house in
Avenue Road, but tho' sitting rooms music room
etc excellent domestic arrangements impossible
we fear we must turn it down. We'd be obliged
to make alterations. which wd be expensive.
W longs to get out of Westminster.
Dined last night with P. M at No 10 to be taken after
by Molly Swinton to Flagstadt concert. Quite genial
+ pleasant. P. M very ready to talk abt. German visits
Thinks, as I gather most people do, that Hitler is
not^ an attractive person, rather common but with
great force of character. Said he wd begin to talk
quietly + then suddenly start ranting, the word
Czech set him off at once, till at last Neville
had to tell him he must stop + let the translator

have a chance or he would never understand
a word. This wd pull him up for a time. Then
part of the technique was for an official to come
in, clicking heels + saluting to hand a paper
to Führer who wd then expclaim, "300 more
Germans killed, how can I wait" + off he
would go again.
I get the impression that Neville talked in the
right way to him, calmly + persistently +
patiently but firmly.
N. cant bear Rippentrop thinks he is no help
but admitted that at the last meeting when he
was accompanying N to Cologne he did do
as N asked + told Hitler that N wd be greatly
helped in opposition at home if he wd say 3
things in his next speech. Which Hitler did
so apparently Rippentrop did give the message.
I think N is quite alive to the opposition. complained
that after coming back so tired when all was over he had
to sit 4 days in H of C - He thinks it is deliberate
trying to wear him out + catch him tripping!
of course it doesnt much matter what Hitler thinks
for no one believes him!
Oxford City won by Quintin Hogg - Lindsay Master of
Balliol seems to have made a very poor show. just
vague criticism no real contribution of a practical kind

Flagstadt has a marvellous voice + great command
of breathing etc. but not nearly as good in
Songs as in opera. Greig she did best. Great
enthusiasm + many encores, she seemed
as unexhausted as the audience!
? Bertie came to lunch, she has stopped taking in Spectator +
now takes a reasonable view on politics She goes over to S. Africa for a bit
Saturday.
Clothes in morning + at 3 go off to Puttenham
Priory to stay with May Harcourt for week end.
Puttenham quite pleasant.
Lady Hudson (ex Lady Northcliffe) Max Müllers + a rather
dull Macnaghten, Guillemards came in to dinner one
night. Nothing really exciting or very interesting. Max Müller
thinks Van's affluent unnecessary I gather, thinks Cadogan
the present head too long suffering in allowing him to keep the
room which belongs to Head of F.O. Van doesnt get all papers
only when matters are referred specially to him.
The Max-Müllers very full of talk about foreign affairs strong
supporters of the P.M's policy.
We stayed till Monday morning. May as always very
affectionate. Looks fairly well only. She must have had
rather a heavy week with Princess Mary herself, Cynthia
Colville + Queen Mary! in Yorkshire. They generally went
out to lunch which was a break, but I gather the evenings

Monday 31st
were very long!
Monday
Mr Gwatkin came to lunch. His right hand very shakey
which distressed, us.
He had had a day in Prague + several days in Berlin.
Thought people wonderful calm in Prague. Told us
that Mr Stopford was going to look after the 10 million loan.
Glad he has got another job. Henderson apparently
not really transferred to F.O. service + not too contented
He said he thought Mr H + Mr Strong were back in P.
He spoke a little of Munich. Was emphatic a to the
personal power of Hitler. He dwarfed everyone else
including Musso who I gather was not impressive
He was not in the room with him only saw him
going to + fro but was very definite as to the impression
he produced.
